observations: Upload progress is a circular SVG ring (role=progressbar, aria-valuenow) with the numeric percent inside it, plus a linear .bar fill and an 'Uploading 10%' badge — graphical with text support, confirmed in loading_desktop.png showing ring '10', green bar, and '10%' label.

Processing status is shown by a three-step Upload→Process→Ready stepper whose dots switch between spinner/check/x SVG icons, an indeterminate striped bar labelled 'Queueing', per-row role=progressbar bars with percent text (8 counted in metrics.graphical.roleProgressbar), and status badges combining an icon (clock/spinner/check/alert via SICON map) with the word Queued/Running/Succeeded/Failed.

Success/failure is graphical everywhere: green 'Succeeded' and red 'Failed' badges with check/alert icons, green/red progress-bar fills (bar s-succeeded / s-failed), red rowmsg banners with a triangle-alert SVG for per-job errors, and a colour-stacked queue summary bar (#stack) splitting queued/running/failed/succeeded by width.
Metrics corroborate: graphical.total = 62 (27 svg, 8 role=progressbar, 27 badges) against only 92 visible words on the whole desktop page.
Raw ratio: 3/3 inventory items graphical+text, 0 text-only, 0 missing.
Whole desktop page is 92 visible words (viewportWords = pageWords = 92); helperWords = 0 and longLeafWords = 0 — there is not a single explanatory paragraph anywhere.
All 11 button labels average 1.55 words with a max of 3 ('Use sample CSV'); longLabels list is empty. Other labels are single words: Retry, Cancel, Download, Discard, Dismiss, Close.
The only guidance copy is the dropzone microcopy 'Drop CSV here / or pick a file' (7 words), which states an affordance the visual alone can't, so it earns its place.
No text restates what the UI shows: status appears once per row as a badge, percent once per bar; error banners carry only the failure reason ('Upstream timeout after 30s'), no preamble.
Two copy issues found, which lands in the '2 to 4 issues' band despite otherwise disciplined writing.

The same entity is named two ways: the panel heading and empty state say 'Runs' / 'No runs yet', while the column header, dialog, and errors say 'Job', 'Job details', 'Job failed', with ids like job_b86738 — no distinct 'run' concept exists in the UI.

Spelling of the same verb is inconsistent: visible notices use American 'Upload canceled' / 'Processing canceled' (resetToIdle strings) while the busy button says 'Cancelling' and the live region says 'Job cancelled'.

Otherwise copy matches behavior exactly: 'Retry' re-issues the call (verified by the async rater, uploadFile 1→2), 'Download' links j.result.downloadUrl with a <jobid>.csv filename, and there is no filler, no marketing tone, and no placeholder text anywhere in the 92 words.

Multiple choices are clearly built for a CSV-processing user: a table/grid glyph used as both logo and dropzone icon, a Rows column with real counts (2,713 / 5,644), JetBrains Mono reserved for machine data (job ids, percentages, row counts, byte sizes), and a 'Use sample CSV' button backed by an actual 9-line embedded orders CSV so the tool is try-able with zero setup.

The Upload→Process→Ready stepper mirrors the brief's exact pipeline, and the 'yours' tag on S.mine job ids distinguishes the user's uploads from other server jobs — a queue-specific decision, not a template one.

The shell, however, is standard dashboard vocabulary: Inter on white cards over a grey page, chip filters with count pills, avatar + plan pill in the header — competent but interchangeable styling, which keeps this off 5.

From the idle desktop screenshot alone: purpose reads instantly as a CSV upload-and-process tool ('CSV Pipeline' wordmark, UPLOAD card with 'Drop CSV here', RUNS table with per-job progress and Download buttons) — matches the brief exactly.
Primary action is unmistakable: the filled green 'Use sample CSV' button inside the dashed dropzone is the only saturated CTA on the page; everything else is outlined or neutral.

What needs attention is equally obvious: three Failed rows with red badges, red partial bars, pink full-width reason banners ('Worker ran out of memory at 1.8 GB', 'Upstream timeout after 30s'), Retry buttons, and a red segment in the queue summary bar.
All three answers verified correct against the brief after reading the source; nothing in the HTML contradicted the screenshot reading.
